status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said McConkey (foot) will practice Wednesday, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
status.longComment: Though he was technically active for this past Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, McConkey wasn't available after failing to practice in any fashion leading up to the contest. Now that he's poised to get back on the practice field Wednesday, McConkey should be in good position to reclaim his usual role as the team's No. 1 wideout this weekend in Kansas City, provided he has no setbacks in his recovery from the foot injury leading up to Sunday. McConkey's potential return is an important development while the Chargers contend with multiple injuries at receiver, as Tre' Harris (hamstring) exited the Week 5 loss early and Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) were inactive for the game.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
status.longComment: Thompson has returned to limited practice after logging consecutive DNPs in the lead-up to the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. The wide receiver did not participate in the contest and the weekend of rest appears to have boosted his recovery process. Thompson will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session to dodge any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Johnston (chest) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report.
status.longComment: A chest injury kept Johnston off the field for Week 5, but he was able to get some work in Wednesday. Fellow pass catchers Ladd McConkey (foot) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) are also banged up -- the latter did not practice Wednesday -- so it remains to be seen what the Los Angeles receiver room will look like Sunday against the Chiefs.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Valdes-Scantling (ribs) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
status.longComment: Valdes-Scantling is dealing with a rib injury that he likely suffered during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. The wide receiver was not given an official injury designation and has already practiced in a limited fashion during the first prep session of Week 6. This indicates that Valdes-Scantling is dealing with a minor injury and will likely be able to suit up for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: The Chargers designated Lambert-Smith (hamstring) for return from injured reserve Tuesday.
status.longComment: The transaction opens up a 21-day window for Lambert-Smith to practice before the Chargers would need to add him to the 53-man roster. If he's able to turn in multiple full practices, Smith-Lambert would stand a decent chance of being activated from IR ahead of Week 6, given the banged-up state of the Chargers receiving corps. Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) all sat out this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, while Tre' Harris (hamstring) exited the game early.

status.label: Doubtful
status.shortComment: Harris (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report.
status.longComment: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is week-to-week with the injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so it comes as little surprise that he did not see any action Wednesday.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) will be out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
status.longComment: Per Ricardo Sandoval of USA Today, Harbaugh told reporters back before Week 1 that he only expected Perryman to spend four games on IR with his unspecified injury, but he'll now be missing his sixth game of the year. Until he's back on the field, veteran Del'Shawn Phillips figures to continue to see increased reps at linebacker.
